cases.answerText: The minimum is **8 feet (2438.4 mm)**, measured from the finished floor to the finished underside of the ceiling or ceiling beams. A living room is habitable space under the supplied definition, and you state that no listed exception applies (BC §§ 202, 1208.2).

cases.label: correct_useful

cases.answerText: A 4-inch horizontal drainage pipe requires a minimum slope of **1/8 inch per foot** (PC § 704.1). Over 40 feet, that is a minimum total fall of **5 inches** (40 × 1/8 inch).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core decision and governing citation match frozen source key.
cases.answerText: Yes. For an attic appliance passageway, the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code exception allows a length up to 50 feet when the passageway is unobstructed and at least 6 feet high and 24 inches wide for its entire length; the stated 30-foot passageway meets that exception’s length and dimension conditions (MC § 306.3). This answers only the length condition, not blanket installation approval.

cases.label: correct_useful

cases.answerText: No. Under the ordinary appliance rule, the shutoff valve must be in the same room and within 6 feet of the appliance. At 8 feet, it exceeds that distance limit; the fact that it is accessible does not change the limit. (2022 NYC FGC § 409.5.1)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core decision and governing citation match frozen source key.
cases.answerText: **No.** The 2022 NYC Fire Code requires yards to be cleaned regularly to prevent rubbish, vegetation, or other combustible waste from accumulating; it does not make cleanup wait until a fire starts or an exit is obstructed (FC § 304.1.1). More generally, causing or allowing rubbish or other combustible waste to accumulate on a premises is unlawful (FC § 304.1). Required means of egress must also be kept continuously free of obstructions and impediments, but that is a separate, ongoing requirement—not the trigger for yard cleanup (FC § 1027.3).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core decision and governing citation match frozen source key.
cases.answerText: **6 enclosed bicycle spaces.** For an ordinary residence subject to the “all other types of residences” row, the rate is 1 space per 2 dwelling units; 11 units yield 5.5 spaces, and fractions of 50% or more count as an additional space. The waiver for buildings or building segments containing 10 dwelling units or less does not apply to 11 units. (ZR § 25-811)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: Yes. Under the 2022 NYC Building Code, glazing in any fixed or operable panel of a swinging door is considered a hazardous location and requires safety glazing, unless an exception applies: an opening too small for a 3-inch sphere to pass, decorative glazing, curved glazing in a revolving door, or a commercial refrigerated-cabinet glazed door (BC §§ 2406.4, 2406.4.1).

cases.answerText: Except for Group R-3 occupancies, an intake on an 18-foot-wide lot must be located at the centerline between the lot lines, because the lot is less than 20 feet wide (MC § 401.4). The same item also states a 10-foot minimum from lot lines or buildings on the same lot; if the opening fronts on a street or public way, measure to that street’s or way’s centerline. The supplied text does not explain how that distance rule applies alongside the centerline rule on an 18-foot-wide lot.

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: **Not under FGC 303.3’s general direct-vent exception:** that exception expressly applies only to rooms other than those used for sleeping. But a narrow, separate rule allows a gas-fired direct-vent space-heating appliance used to heat a sleeping room to be deemed outside the room **if** the appliance and installation comply with FGC 303.3.1.1 through 303.3.1.7. (FGC §§ 303.3, 303.3.1.) The supplied text sets some of those conditions, but omits § 303.3.1.6, so whether a particular appliance qualifies cannot be fully determined from this packet.

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: **No.** FC 305.2 expressly prohibits depositing hot ashes in a combustible container. Its exception allows a 2-foot separation from other combustible materials only when the material is deposited in a **covered, noncombustible container** placed on a noncombustible floor, ground surface, or stand; it does not permit a combustible container. (FC § 305.2)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: No. In all Manufacturing Districts, ZR 43-22 says a yard or rear yard equivalent may not be higher than curb level, but expressly says compliance does not require disturbing natural grade. The section also limits structures above ground level in required yards, subject to the permitted-obstruction provisions in ZR 43-23. (ZR § 43-22)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: **The minimum is 8 feet (2,438.4 mm)**, measured from the finished floor to the finished underside of the ceiling. The 2022 NYC Building Code sets that minimum for habitable rooms and spaces; a living room in a dwelling unit is habitable space. You’ve stated that no basement, mezzanine, or beam exception applies. (BC §§ 1208.2, 202)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: For a straight, uniform 40-foot run of 4-inch horizontal drainage pipe, the minimum slope is **1/8 inch per foot**, requiring **5 inches of total fall** (40 × 1/8). The 4-inch pipe falls in Table 704.1’s 3-to-6-inch size range; the code requires uniform alignment and uniform slope (PC § 704.1).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: Yes. Under the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code, a 30-foot attic passageway meets the exception’s length condition if it is unobstructed and at least 6 feet high and 24 inches wide along its entire length: the exception allows up to 50 feet. The stated dimensions and length satisfy those conditions; this answers only the length limit, not blanket installation approval (MC § 306.3).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and citation match frozen key and scope addendum.
cases.answerText: **No.** Under the ordinary rule, the shutoff valve must be within 6 feet of the appliance; being in the same room and accessible does not satisfy that separate distance limit. At 8 feet, it is too far away (2022 NYC FGC § 409.5.1).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and source scope match frozen key.
cases.answerText: No. An open yard must be regularly cleaned to prevent the accumulation of rubbish, vegetation, or other combustible waste; the rule does not make cleaning conditional on a fire or an obstructed exit (FC § 304.1.1). Separately, rubbish and other combustible waste may not be allowed to accumulate on a premises (FC § 304.1).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and source scope match frozen key.
cases.answerText: **Six bicycle spaces.** ZR 25-811 sets the rate for ordinary residences at 1 space per 2 dwelling units, and counts a fraction of a space of 50% or more as an additional space. For 11 units: 11 ÷ 2 = 5.5, rounded up to **6**—but the same section waives the table requirement for a building or building segment containing 10 dwelling units or less. Since this building has 11 units and you state no other waiver applies, the requirement is **6 enclosed accessory bicycle spaces**. (ZR § 25-811)

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and source scope match frozen key.
cases.answerText: Yes. Under the 2022 NYC Building Code, glazing in all fixed and operable panels of swinging, sliding, and bifold doors is considered a hazardous location. Exceptions include openings too small for a 3-inch-diameter sphere to pass through, decorative glazing, curved glazed panels in revolving doors, and commercial refrigerated-cabinet glazed doors (BC § 2406.4.1).

cases.label: correct_useful
cases.note: Core conclusion and source scope match frozen key.
cases.answerText: No. Under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, a shower compartment must be at least 900 square inches in interior cross-sectional area **and** at least 30 inches in its least finished-interior dimension; 950 square inches satisfies the area minimum, but 28 inches does not satisfy the separate dimension minimum (PC § 417.4). The specified measurement excludes fixture valves, showerheads, soap dishes, and safety grab bars or rails. The provision also says that, except as required in Section 404, both measurements are taken at the stated threshold-level location and continued to at least 70 inches above the shower-drain outlet; the supplied text does not include Section 404, so its possible effect on applying that measurement rule cannot be resolved here.

Separately, FGC § 303.3.1 deems a gas-fired direct-vent space-heating appliance used to heat a sleeping room to be located outside the room, but only if the appliance and its installation comply with §§ 303.3.1.1 through 303.3.1.7. Direct-vent status alone does not meet that condition.

Its exception allows a 2-foot separation from other combustible materials only when the ashes are deposited in a covered, noncombustible container on a noncombustible floor, ground surface, or stand; it does not permit a combustible container. (FC § 305.2)
